name: Sulfur
occurrence: Found free as native sulfur near volcanic and hot-spring deposits, and combined in sulfide/sulfate minerals.
majorUses: Sulfuric acid production (the world's most-manufactured industrial chemical)
biologicalRelevance: Present in two amino acids (cysteine and methionine) and forms the disulfide bonds that hold protein structures like hair keratin together.
notableCharacteristics: Exists in more allotropic forms than almost any other element, most commonly as bright yellow S₈ rings.
whyHere: Six valence electrons like oxygen above it, but a much larger atom favours forming S₈ ring structures rather than a simple diatomic gas, which is why sulfur is a yellow solid while oxygen is a colourless gas.
didYouKnow: The disulfide bonds sulfur forms in keratin are literally what a perm or hair-straightening treatment breaks and reshapes chemically.
genZNote: The reason your perm holds and your eggs smell weird. Underrated MVP of protein structure.
